body:
How RecallSegmenter builds the graph

RecallSegmenter is a deterministic, rule-based baseline. It first indexes the exact transcript as sentences and tokens. It then cuts sentences into short recall units at cues such as semicolons, "and then", "because", and "before that", while retaining the exact character span and text of every unit.

For each unit, fixed cue lists assign a discourse function, record hedging such as "I think", and build a shallow sketch of the likely action, participants, polarity, modality, locations, and sensory words. Names and person phrases become recall entities. Repeated noun phrases and nearby compatible pronouns create simple coreference links. Connectives between neighboring units create temporal or causal edges.

RecallGraph.validated then checks the bookkeeping: every span lies inside the transcript and reproduces its text exactly; ids and ordinals are coherent; relation endpoints exist; and every participant reference points to a known recall entity. A checked graph therefore certifies structural and textual consistency. Linguistic accuracy remains an empirical question.

In the example, "and they lifted him into the boat" becomes a second unit because "and" followed by a pronoun is one of the split cues. The fixed lexicons recognize lift, they, him, and boat. This explains both the two-unit output and the visible limitation later on the page, where the shallow sketch reads "got hit" as get. A future parser or provider can replace that shallow analysis while preserving the same checked graph contract.

I volunteer to turn this into a lucid "How it works" section on method/represent-recall, or a short linked page, once the documentation bead owner gives me the source checkout/path and exact assignment. I have not edited generated docs-site/dist or another actors preview tree.
